tells.1: The named success story feels inserted to signal authenticity rather than integrated into the description.
tells.2: Generic promotional filler: “keep your recovery moving” and “get more of what the app has to offer.”
tells.3: Stacked reassurance and stock marketing phrases: “guidance you can trust,” “keep you on track,” and “unlock more.”

reason: Version 4 reads like restrained, purposeful editing: concrete features, clear audience, and little filler, though it should explain what Premium includes. Version 1 has the most distinctive voice and a useful paid-feature description, but its awkward opening and unsupported recovery anecdote weaken its readiness to publish; these stylistic judgments do not establish authorship.
